LGPLv3 section 4 replacement/recombination method
Published Firefox 1.0.0 XPI inspected 28 October 2026; static verification

Section 4(d)(0) requires both Minimal Corresponding Source for the library and
Corresponding Application Code in a suitable form and under terms allowing
recombination. Application code may be object and/or source code, with necessary
data and utilities. A public ExtPay source repository alone is insufficient.
Section 4(d)(1) is not assumed merely because vendor/ExtPay.js is a separate file.

Application material is the published XPI identified in RELEASE-SOURCE-MAP.json:
its HTML/JavaScript/assets/manifest are readable and can be copied independently
of the original edition packager. An interface-compatible vendor/ExtPay.js can
therefore be substituted without compiling the proprietary application anew.
Static inspection confirms the separate library manifest entries and delivered
application files; no application compiler or private packaging utility is needed
to substitute the library. The shipped vendor/NOTICE.txt grants replacement,
recombination and debugging rights with precedence over conflicting application
terms. This supports the section 4(d)(0) technical route; it is not legal
certification or a newly executed modified-library browser test. Do not upload
proprietary application code or XPIs here or infer a general application source
licence. This assessment covers public Free 1.0.0, not internal Pro builds.

Recipient process:
1. Obtain covered source through NOTICES.txt. Obtain the exact corresponding
   TenantTabs XPI only through its authorised distribution, not this repository.
2. Modify ExtPay.dev.js, rebuilding the library as described in build-instructions.txt,
   or use an interface-compatible modified ExtPay IIFE under its applicable terms.
3. Extract a copy of the authorised XPI into a separate development directory.
   Retain the application manifest/assets and replace vendor/ExtPay.js only.
   The existing manifest loads that path for background/content-script use.
   Keep the global ExtPay name/public API. Record changes and retain notices.
4. Discard stale META-INF signature files only in the working copy. The original
   publisher signature cannot authenticate modified content. Do not change the
   installed original, claim an official modified release or use publisher keys.
5. In an isolated Firefox development profile use about:debugging / This Firefox /
   Load Temporary Add-on and select the extracted manifest.json. Mozilla documents
   this supported temporary execution route. It ends on removal/browser restart
   and does not fully reproduce permanent signed installation. No preference
   change, signing bypass or publisher service credential is required for this
   temporary step. It is not proof of final LGPL installation compliance.

Firefox signing limits
Release/beta permanent installation requires Mozilla signing. A recipient cannot
reuse the publisher's signature after replacing the library. A separately signed
modified add-on would require the recipient's own suitable ID/account and Mozilla
review; approval, identity continuity and user-data migration are not guaranteed.
Mozilla also documents configuration-dependent unsigned installation in certain
development channels, but this preparation changes no Firefox preference and
does not treat such a configuration change as an established compliance solution.
The TenantTabs qualification signing helper intentionally cannot sign arbitrary
recipient IDs. Signing through the publisher is not a condition of these rights.

Section 4(e) / GPLv3 section 6 installation information
The GPL User Product provision is conditional, including a conveyance in/with/
specifically for a User Product as part of a transfer of possession/use of that
product. A standalone extension download on the recipient's existing computer
does not by itself establish such a transfer; distributing with hardware or a
different transaction could change the analysis. Neither universal exemption
nor automatic applicability is asserted here. For the published standalone
Firefox download, no transfer of possession/use of a User Product has been
identified, so no additional installation information has been identified under
this conditional provision. This assesses that distribution only. If applicable, sufficient
installation/execution information is needed; a session-only load or a route
dependent on unguaranteed third-party signing must not be silently approved.
Even if section 4(e) does not apply, section 4(d)(0)'s materials and effective
permission requirements still apply. Copyright attribution permission is not a
blanket waiver of any of these other obligations.

Release scope
RELEASE-SOURCE-MAP.json identifies the inspected public XPI and library sources.
Future releases must retain effective permissions, notices and corresponding
materials and update that mapping. Distribution with hardware or under different
terms requires reassessment. No publisher credentials or general proprietary
redistribution rights are supplied by this method. This does not reopen the
resolved LGPL/AGPL ambiguity or certify legal compliance.
